text:
A VPN is a private tunnel between your device and another computer on the internet, and all your traffic goes through it.

Normally, websites see your address and your internet provider can see where you go. With a VPN, your data is locked (encrypted) before it leaves your device. It travels to the VPN company's computer, which then talks to the website for you. The website sees the VPN's address, not yours, and your provider only sees scrambled data going to the VPN.

It helps on public Wi-Fi, hides your location from websites, and keeps your provider from seeing what you browse. It doesn't make you fully anonymous, since the VPN company can still see your activity, so pick one you trust.
